concerns.text: The plan assumes the existence of external Zenodo/HuggingFace datasets containing pre-computed wavefunction coefficients for 1D Heisenberg and Ising models with spin counts 10-40. No specific dataset ID, URL, or repository is cited. The fallback to internal generation (Exact Diagonalization/DMRG) is described as a 'fallback' but is the only feasible path for N>20 on CPU. Relying on non-existent external data for the primary hypothesis test (N=10-40) renders the plan infeasible as written; the 'Verified Datasets' block is empty of actual sources.

The research plan states: 'If no open, directly downloadable dataset exists... the pipeline will fail gracefully... No synthetic data will be used to replace real simulation data for the primary correlation test.' This creates a logical contradiction with the feasibility constraints. Generating 'real' wavefunctions for N=40 via Exact Diagonalization is computationally impossible (2^40 state vector). The plan must explicitly commit to internal generation (ED for N<=20, DMRG for N>20) as the primary data source, not a fallback, to satisfy the N=10-40 scope.

The plan cites 'scipy.sparse.linalg.svds' as a potential solution for memory constraints but does not specify the target sparsity or the specific algorithm (e.g., Lanczos) to be used for the reduced density matrix SVD. While not a dataset error, the lack of a concrete strategy for the 'sparse/streaming' claim in the context of 2^20 matrices makes the compute feasibility claim unverifiable.
